A 28-year-old woman visits her doctor for a routine pap smear. During the evaluation, she expresses
frustration about being unable to engage in sexual intercourse with her boyfriend. She states that she
feels safe and interested in intimacy with him, but experiences severe pain during vaginal penetration,
which forces them to stop. She has no significant medical history and denies other associated
symptoms. Her vital signs are within normal limits: temperature 97.4°F (36.1°C), blood pressure 114/76
mmHg, pulse 69/min, and respirations 12/min. Physical examination reveals no abnormalities, trauma,
or pain in the vulva or vagina, and the speculum exam is unremarkable. A bimanual examination shows
no uterine abnormalities, and comprehensive laboratory tests are normal. What is the most appropriate
treatment for this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Cognitive behavioral therapy (B) Ceftriaxone (C)
Sildenafil (D) Sexual therapy with partner involvement (E) Dilator therapy (F) Pelvic floor physical
therapy (G) Anxiolytic medication (H) Botulinum toxin injection (I) Topical lidocaine application (J)
